clue.text: Jolly Jack, first to come in like Humpty Dumpty

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: to come in tells us one piece is entered into the middle of another

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme egg is egg-shaped, which is oval
I is the Roman numeral one, and one means first

explanation.surface: A cheerful sailor, first to arrive, looks as round as Humpty Dumpty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come in' puts I inside OVAL, giving OVIAL after the J.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a cheerful, good-humoured person, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Wanderer, former invader, right across the front page

indicators.note: across says the invader stretches over the page, with it inside

parts.note: the Jutes were among the Germanic tribes that invaded Britain
the front page is page one: P for page and I for one

explanation.surface: An old invader's story runs right across the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means the invader's name straddles the front page. The Jutes came from Jutland and settled in Kent. 'Wanderer' is a planet, as throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet comes from the Greek for wanderer, and this is the largest planet in the solar system.

clue.text: Wanderer with seamen on the "Victory" in Europe?

indicators.note: on joins the two pieces, the seamen coming after

parts.note: VE day marked Victory in Europe in 1945
NUS was the National Union of Seamen

explanation.surface: A traveller sails with the crew aboard HMS Victory somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make 'Victory' look like Nelson's ship, but it is the V of VE day. The planet is the second from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet comes from the Greek for wanderer, and this is the planet nearest Earth.

clue.text: I prevent recall of seaman I discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered suggests the letters are uncovered and turned out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor stops a memory coming back of the seaman someone found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' rearranges SEAMANI. The definition speaks as the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the condition that stops a person from recalling things, so it can say this of itself.

clue.text: Wanderer from end to end not having enough

indicators.note: from end tells us to take the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: planet comes from the Greek for wanderer, and this puzzle's planets are all called that; ours is the third from the sun

explanation.surface: A traveller roaming from one end of the land to the other runs short of supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle 'Wanderer' means a planet (Greek planetes, wanderer). The closing letter of 'end' is D.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or lack of something is the state of not having enough of it.

clue.text: Point to ask about royal attendant

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

indicators.note: about says the word for asking surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to query means to ask
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone directs a question to a member of the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside QUERY, making QUERRY, after E. An equerry attends a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who attends a member of the British royal family.

clue.text: Runner careers wildly round house

indicators.note: round says the scrambled letters surround the abbreviation for house
wildly says the letters fly about in a new order

explanation.surface: A competitor charges about recklessly near a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' gives RACERSE from the runner-like verb, and 'round' wraps it about the house; 'careers' looks like the verb of the surface but is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse entered in a race is called a runner.

clue.text: Captive male embracing male with love

indicators.note: embracing says the pronoun holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
love means zero in tennis, hence O
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A captive man hugs another man, with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the pronoun round the rest; 'with' simply joins love to the second male. Love is zero from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive, so the noun matches the noun sense of captive.

clue.text: Tibetan dish gives time to dance

parts.note: the samba is a Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: A Tibetan meal gives you time to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsamba is roasted barley flour, a staple food of Tibet.

clue.text: What to do before and after packing? There's no doubt about it

definitions.text: What to do before and after packing
definitions.meaning: you open the suitcase, pack it, then shut it
a matter so plain that it needs no argument

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a matter settled beyond doubt, and literally describes handling a suitcase.

clue.text: Arrest of secret police?

parts.note: the Stasi was the secret police of communist East Germany
of gives the possessive ending, an apostrophe and S, belonging to the police

explanation.surface: A question about the detention carried out by a secret police force.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'of secret police' as the possessive STASI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrest can mean a stopping or standstill, as in cardiac arrest, which is a state of no movement.

clue.text: Wanderer treated gash with methane

parts.note: planet comes from the Greek for wanderer; the red planet is the fourth from the sun

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters of the wound are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A planet's inhabitant dresses a cut with methane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges GASH into HGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the gas given off by rotting vegetation in swamps, so the two are names for the same gas.

clue.text: Rejection of painting by acknowledgement of opera

indicators.note: rejection here means throwing back, so the word for painting is turned backwards

parts.note: painting is a kind of art
via means by way of
TA is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: A painting is turned down after being acknowledged by an opera company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejection of' turns ART into TRA. LA TRAVIATA is Verdi's opera, here without its article.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's La Traviata is one of the most famous operas, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Live edict upsetting to wit

indicators.note: upsetting suggests knocking the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A live decree upsets people, namely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges LIVEEDICT. Videlicet is Latin, shortened to viz.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet is Latin for namely, the same as the phrase meaning that is to say.

clue.text: In olden days king met king at ball

indicators.note: In at the front places the first king inside the phrase for old times

parts.note: yore means times long past
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Long ago one monarch met another at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A YORKER is a cricket delivery aimed to land at the batsman's feet. 'ball' looks like a dance but is a cricket ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a yorker is a type of delivery, so the answer is a kind of ball bowled.

clue.text: Method kept back from jumbo seat

parts.note: how means the way or method of doing something

indicators.note: kept back tells us the word for retained is written backwards

parts.note: had means kept or held

explanation.surface: A technique withheld from someone's large chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HAD into DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is the canopied seat fixed on an elephant's back, and jumbo is a nickname for an elephant.

clue.text: Nothing to do with endless wake having scent

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
do is the verb itself

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to rouse is to wake

explanation.surface: Something smelly, not at all connected with a tired awakening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ROUSE to ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means giving off a smell, so it means having scent.

clue.text: Animal responsible for the wanderer of 11 or Ms Wanderer of 4

indicators.note: responsible for suggests these letters make the animal when rearranged

parts.note: the planet in 11 across is the red planet

explanation.surface: A small pet is behind the planet in one answer or Miss Earth in another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' means these letters produce the animal when rearranged. The words after 'or' offer a second route: MS with the planet of 4 across rearranges the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent kept as a pet, an example of an animal.

clue.text: "President" and "limit", for example?

parts.note: the two quoted words are a pair of vocabulary items; also, an American president is limited to two periods in office

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a pair of words and also the US limit on a president's spells in office.

clue.text: One or two containers for South American in Tennessee

indicators.note: in says the South American goes inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee
the Incas were the people of the Andean empire

explanation.surface: Containers for a Peruvian living in Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two containers' works because the answer is one container whose name joins two words for containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin can is a single container, but tin and can are each also words for containers.

clue.text: Leaves right away on 1st of October, late

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the following piece below the first
1st of picks the opening letter of the month
right away says the abbreviation for right is taken out

parts.note: verdure means green foliage

explanation.surface: Leaves turn and go on the first of October, behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from VERDURE to leave VERDUE, under O.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past the expected time, so it means late.

clue.text: Wanderer in tube?

definitions.meaning: planet comes from the Greek for wanderer; this is the one nearest the sun
the liquid metal sits in the glass tube of a thermometer or barometer

explanation.definitionFit: The innermost planet shares its name with the metal used in thermometer tubes.

clue.text: Lacking public relations is a difficulty in granny's being in the upper house

indicators.note: in places the shortened difficulty inside the word for grandmother

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for granny

indicators.note: lacking says the following letters are missing from the word that comes after

parts.note: a problem is a difficulty

explanation.surface: Without good publicity, it's hard for Grandma to get into the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' leaves OBLEM, which 'in' places inside granny's name. The upper house is the House of Lords in Britain's parliament, where hereditary peers once sat.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer such as a duke or earl, a member of the British aristocracy, sits in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Dispose of old wine

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Throw away some old wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To export goods is to sell them abroad, which is one way of disposing of them.

clue.text: Wanderer parking at nameless airport

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

indicators.note: nameless says the abbreviation for name is lost from the word

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London

explanation.surface: A traveller parks at an unnamed airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' takes N for name out of LUTON. The planet is now classed as a dwarf planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet comes from the Greek for wanderer, and this was long counted the ninth planet.

clue.text: Bach piece to former president sounds undue fag, sadly

indicators.note: sounds says we want what the words are like when spoken

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president; to plus his name, said in a British accent

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters which follow are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A piece of music dedicated to an ex-president sounds like a dreadful chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Carter' spoken without the R sounds like TOCCATA. 'sadly' rearranges UNDUEFAG into ANDFUGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Toccata and Fugue in D minor is a famous organ work by J S Bach.

clue.text: Wanderer assumed position on vessel

indicators.note: on joins the two pieces, the first coming before the second

parts.note: to sit is to take up a position, so sat means assumed a position
an urn is a kind of vessel

explanation.surface: Someone took a seat on a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: As throughout, 'Wanderer' is a planet; this is the ringed one.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet comes from the Greek for wanderer, and this one is the sixth from the sun.

clue.text: Wrong iron left with some irony

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: some tells us to take only part of the following word

explanation.surface: A mistaken iron tool left lying about with a touch of irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ONY from 'irony'.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime, a wrong in the legal sense of the noun.
